_comment: issue M6-09 LogQL-pipeline differential corpus + coverage matrix (e2e/src/logs_corpus.rs + e2e/src/logs.rs). `{R}` in every case's `query` is replaced with this run's run_id at execution time; every case conjoins `run_id="{R}"` plus a `service_name` scope pinning the body shape its parser expects, so a stale stack can never leak foreign streams into a set-equality comparison. Gate discipline (traces precedent, plan v3 delta 5): every stage has >= 1 case, every case starts `mode: "gated"`, and the exclusion list starts EMPTY. A case moves to `mode: "informational"` only via the triage discipline — an observed live divergence, classified fix-our-bug vs ratify-documented-oracle-delta, recorded in docs/benchmarks/logs-differential-ledger.md (the `ledger` field names the entry); PulsusDB stays hard-gated against the corpus expectation even then. `limit` is the query_range request cap on both stores; every case's expected entry set is sized strictly below it (validity gates in logs.rs).

issue #99: a `| json` over a non-object line errors — the stream carries __error__=JSONParserErr plus the byte-exact __error_details__, compared set-equal against grafana/loki:3.4.2

issue #99: `| __error__ != ""` keeps the errored stream, carrying BOTH __error__ and __error_details__ (the drop side `| __error__ = ""` is a Tier-1 hermetic golden — an empty differential set is not a valid set comparison)
issue #99: `| logfmt | n > 5` fails the numeric conversion — LabelFilterErr plus the byte-exact Go strconv.ParseFloat detail

issue #100: fetch-until-limit ordered-limited case. `| json | status = "503" | took_ms = "500"` is two dropping label filters (fetch_until_limit, scan_limit = limit*factor = 40) whose earliest-limit=4 svc-json survivors (j=9,29,49,69) span >= 2 keyset pages: page 1 (earliest 40 svc-json rows, j in [0,39]) yields only 2 survivors (j=9,29) < 4, forcing a second fetch; page 2 (j in [40,79]) adds j=49,69 to fill at exactly 4. j=9 and j=69 are both GET /api/users 503 500 => the SAME stream carrying two entries, so their arrival order is a real per-stream ordering property. Compared as an ORDERED earliest-4 Vec<(labels,ts,line)> (per-stream ascending verified as received, then k-way merged) against grafana/loki:3.4.2; raw==limit==4 is the page-2 proof. Full tier only (self-gated in run_streams_limited_case).

issue #109: an OTLP log record's InstrumentationScope lands in per-entry structured metadata (Loki 3.4.2 parity, not indexed stream labels). `| scope_name="coll-scope"` is a structured-metadata pipeline filter selecting the single collision-bearing svc-scope witness; the flattened response (last-write-wins collision resolution: dup_key=v_us, scope_name=coll-scope beating scope.name=LOSE, scope_version=1.0) is compared set-equal PulsusDB==grafana/loki:3.4.2. run_streams_case additionally asserts the {scope_name="coll-scope"} STREAM selector returns empty on both stores (the placement discriminator). A fourth scope attribute carrying an empty VALUE was removed by the #259 reopen: the oracle at 3.4.2 keeps an empty attribute value while the pinned reference grafana/loki:3.7.4 and PulsusDB drop it, so no such input can match on both stores — docs/benchmarks/logs-differential-ledger.md `empty-value-oracle-version-skew`.

issue #201: `| logfmt | addr = ip("10.0.0.0/8")` — a missing `addr` label DROPS the line (no __error__). The svc-ipmiss scope carries one witness with a matching in-range addr (returned) and one lacking addr (dropped), so the set is NON-EMPTY and proves the drop rule

issue #201: `| logfmt | addr != ip("10.0.0.0/8")` — a present-but-non-IP `addr` value is a plain non-match (the IP label filter NEVER errors), so `!=` RETURNS the svc-ipbad witness carrying only its raw `addr=not-an-ip` label and NO __error__/__error_details__, compared set-equal against reference v3.7.3, the oracle pinned at the time (now v3.7.4; this is a value record, not a claim about the current pin)

cases.construct: M8-LQ3 rate_counter over a resetting unwrapped counter (c=10,30,5,12 by ts, samples 1s apart ⇒ span 3s): reset-aware increase 32, scaled by the reference's ns-as-ms extrapolation factor (1 + 60000/span_ns; extrapolatedRate divides ns spans by 1000, window anchored on the first sample), then / 60s window = 0.5333439999999999 (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3). Instant [1m] lookback — semantically identical on both stores (issue #227's sliding range grid does not apply)

M8-LQ3 rate_counter over sparse interior samples (c=200,260 at offsets 10,11 ⇒ 1s apart, span 1s): increase 60, scaled by the reference's ns-as-ms extrapolation factor (1 + 60000/span_ns), then / 60s window = 1.00006 (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3). This is NOT Prometheus full-range extrapolation (which would inflate to ~6.0) — the ns/ms unit mix keeps durationToStart at 60, so the factor is ~1.00006, not ~6

M8-LQ3 rate_counter over a monotone counter (c=100,160 at offsets 12,13 ⇒ 1s apart, span 1s): increase 60, scaled by the reference's ns-as-ms extrapolation factor (1 + 60000/span_ns), then / 60s window = 1.00006 (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3). The half-open (t-range, t] edge-inclusion rule is pinned in the hermetic reducer golden

M8-LQ3 rate_counter duplicate-timestamp handling: samples 5,{10,3}@one-ts,12 (offsets 14,15,15,16 ⇒ span 2s) processed in delivered scan order (ts asc, then body asc) as 5,10,3,12 — +5, reset +3, +9 = increase 17, scaled by the reference's ns-as-ms extrapolation factor (1 + 60000/span_ns), then / 60s window = 0.2833418333333333 (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3; an ascending-VALUE tie-sort would wrongly give the 12-based value). Both stores order same-ts samples in storage order, not by value

M8-LQ3 sort value-ordering: sort(sum by (grp) (count_over_time(...))) over counts {a:5,b:1,c:5} returns the vector ascending by value with the a/c tie broken by label ascending — order b,a,c (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3). Set-equal validity gate plus a store-vs-store ordered-sequence gate (metric_instant_ordered)

M8-LQ3 sort_desc value-ordering: sort_desc(sum by (grp) (count_over_time(...))) over the SAME counts {a:5,b:1,c:5} returns the vector DESCENDING by value with the a/c tie broken by label ascending — order a,c,b (oracle-confirmed v3.7.3). Independent end-to-end coverage of the sort_desc handler/encoder path. Set-equal validity gate plus a store-vs-store ordered-sequence gate (metric_instant_ordered)
